First Harvest Estimate Points To Larger Wheat And Oat Supplies

OSTARA, Kestria, Aug. 19, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative estimates that its members will harvest 184,000 tonnes of wheat and 52,000 tonnes of oats this season. The figures cover 426 farms across Kestria and are based on field inspections, planted area records and reports submitted by members up to 18 August.

The wheat estimate is 8 per cent above last season's final total, while oats are estimated to rise by 5 per cent. Fields around Amberford have the strongest yield prospects. Crops near Ostara show more variation following a dry spell during grain development.

These are field estimates, rather than grain already available for sale. Rain, harvesting conditions and the amount retained on farms may affect deliveries. Buyers seeking wheat or oats can obtain indicative supply information from the co-operative's sales desks in Amberford, Kestrel Bay and Saltmarsh.

Amberford Receiving Yard Introduces Separate Queues For Wheat And Oats

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Aug. 21, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has introduced separate wheat and oat queues at its Amberford receiving yard. The change follows a trial involving 38 deliveries, during which the average time from arrival to unloading fell from 54 minutes to 37 minutes. Both lanes use the existing weighbridge.

Drivers must identify their crop and booking reference at the entrance before joining a queue. Loads still require sampling, weighing and acceptance checks. A separate holding area is available for vehicles whose grain needs further testing, allowing other accepted loads to move through the yard.

The yard has received 2,640 tonnes of new-season grain so far, mostly wheat from farms south of Amberford. Members without a booking should contact the receiving office before travelling. The co-operative has also added clear signs at the approach road and pedestrian crossing beside the sampling room.

Early Wheat Samples Show Firm Protein And Low Moisture

OSTARA, Kestria, Sept. 7, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- The first new-season quality report from Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative shows average wheat protein of 12.6 per cent and average moisture of 13.2 per cent. The report covers 186 accepted loads, representing 5,920 tonnes delivered to the Amberford and Ostara receiving sites by 6 September.

Average wheat test weight was 78.4 kilogrammes per hectolitre. These results support the sale of several parcels for milling, although each customer contract has its own requirements. The samples mainly represent earlier-harvested fields and should not be treated as a measure of the whole crop.

Oat deliveries remain limited, with 740 tonnes accepted so far. Members can request the test results for their own loads through the receiving office. Any request for a second test must identify the delivery ticket, allowing staff to locate the sealed sample retained from that load.

September Purchase Notice Sets Wheat And Oat Base Prices

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Sept. 14, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has set its posted purchase price at KRN 286 per tonne for standard milling wheat and KRN 218 per tonne for standard food oats. The prices apply to new purchase agreements accepted from 14 September for grain delivered to the Amberford receiving site.

The wheat price assumes moisture no higher than 14 per cent and protein of at least 12 per cent. The oat price assumes moisture no higher than 13.5 per cent and test weight of at least 52 kilogrammes per hectolitre. Other quality requirements remain available from the buying desk.

These are prices paid to supplying members, rather than delivered selling prices for customers. Haulage, drying and any agreed quality adjustments are shown separately on settlement statements. Existing fixed-price agreements retain their agreed terms. Members should obtain a purchase reference before sending grain against the new notice.

Rain Raises Drying Demand At Ostara Grain Receiving Site

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 16, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Rain around Ostara has increased the proportion of wheat deliveries requiring drying at Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's local receiving site. Of the 61 wheat loads sampled during the past two days, 24 exceeded the standard moisture limit of 14 per cent. Accepted wet grain is being stored separately.

The site's dryer has processed 460 tonnes since the rain began. Members are being given a moisture reading and an estimated drying charge before unloading. The charge depends on the moisture removed and is separate from the purchase price shown on the member's grain agreement.

Receiving staff have reduced the number of wet-grain bookings to match drying capacity. Dry wheat and oat bookings remain available, subject to storage space. Members should report their latest moisture reading when arranging a delivery and should not mix damp grain with a dry load to meet the acceptance limit.

Harvest Review Trims Wheat Estimate As Oat Outlook Holds

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Sept. 28, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has revised its member wheat harvest estimate to 179,500 tonnes, down from the August estimate of 184,000 tonnes. The oat estimate is now 52,400 tonnes, compared with 52,000 tonnes previously. The review uses completed field records and updated reports received by 27 September.

Lower wheat yields around Ostara account for most of the reduction. Amberford results remain close to the earlier estimate. Members report that 81 per cent of their wheat area and 69 per cent of their oat area has been harvested, leaving uncertainty around the remaining fields.

The co-operative has accepted 96,800 tonnes of wheat and 21,600 tonnes of oats into its stores. These intake figures exclude grain still held on farms and must not be added to the harvest estimate. Customer allocations remain covered by accepted stocks and grain secured under existing member delivery agreements.

Kestrel Bay Loading Repairs Restore Normal Grain Dispatch Capacity

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 6, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has restored normal dispatch capacity at its Kestrel Bay store after replacing a worn bearing in the grain loading conveyor. The conveyor returned to service on 5 October following an inspection and an unloaded test. Grain receiving continued while the equipment was unavailable.

The interruption delayed nine customer collections carrying a combined 270 tonnes of wheat and oats. Six have now been completed, and revised collection times have been agreed for the remaining three. No grain was damaged, and the affected conveyor did not require any stored stock to be discarded.

The loading line is again operating at its normal rate of up to 90 tonnes an hour, subject to vehicle changes and sampling. Customers should use the collection time shown on their latest dispatch confirmation. Drivers arriving early must wait in the marked parking area until called to the loading point.

New Oat Quality Report Supports Food Processing Orders

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 12, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's latest oat quality report records an average test weight of 54.8 kilogrammes per hectolitre and average moisture of 12.9 per cent. The results cover 18,300 tonnes sampled across its Amberford, Ostara and Val-Brume stores. Each reported parcel has completed intake testing.

Screenings averaged 2.1 per cent by weight. Of the volume covered, 16,700 tonnes met the co-operative's standard food oat specification without further cleaning. The remaining 1,600 tonnes has been identified separately for cleaning or sale against a different specification. Customer requirements are checked before an order is confirmed.

Buyers can request parcel summaries showing moisture, test weight and screenings from the sales desk. A summary describes the sampled grain and does not replace the specification in a sales agreement. Retained samples are available for additional agreed checks where a processor needs more information before accepting a parcel.

Val-Brume Office Adds French Language Grain Settlement Statements

OSTARA, Kestria, Oct. 13, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative now offers French-language grain settlement statements through its Val-Brume office. Members can choose French or English for statements covering wheat and oat purchases. The service follows requests from 47 members in Kestria's French-speaking region and a review of the terms used on existing documents.

Each statement shows the accepted weight, agreed purchase price, quality adjustments, service charges and net payment in Kestrian crowns. Delivery ticket numbers appear beside the relevant entries so members can compare a settlement with their receiving records. The calculation method is the same in both languages.

Members can register their language preference by telephone or in person at the Val-Brume office. Copies of earlier statements can also be requested in either language. Staff have checked 120 sample statements against the underlying purchase records, including transactions with drying charges and deliveries settled across more than one payment.

Wheat Purchase Price Rises As Milling Demand Strengthens

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 15, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has raised its posted purchase price for standard milling wheat to KRN 294 per tonne, an increase of KRN 8 from its September notice. The standard food oat price remains KRN 218 per tonne. Both prices apply to new agreements accepted from 15 October at Amberford.

The wheat adjustment reflects stronger enquiries from millers in Saltmarsh and Kestrel Bay, alongside a smaller supply of uncommitted wheat meeting their specifications. The co-operative has signed sales agreements for 6,200 tonnes of milling wheat during the first half of October. Prices in individual customer agreements remain confidential.

The standard quality thresholds in the September purchase notice remain in place. Haulage, drying and quality adjustments continue to be listed separately. Existing fixed-price member agreements are unchanged. Members considering a sale can request a written calculation showing the applicable base price and any charges for their proposed delivery.

Completed Harvest Returns Confirm Wheat And Oat Crop Totals

AMBERFORD, Kestria, Oct. 20, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Completed harvest returns from all 426 supplying farms put Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative's member crop at 180,200 tonnes of wheat and 53,100 tonnes of oats. The totals replace the estimates issued in September. Wheat production was 5.8 per cent above last season, while oat production rose by 7.2 per cent.

The final wheat figure is 700 tonnes above the September estimate, with later Amberford fields contributing most of the difference. Oats finished 700 tonnes above the revised estimate. Members supplied harvested area and weighed production records, with separate estimates for the small amount of grain retained in unweighed farm bins.

Co-operative stores have received 158,600 tonnes of wheat and 44,800 tonnes of oats from this harvest. The balance remains on farms for later delivery, farm use or other sales. Production totals describe the member crop and do not represent the quantity available for immediate purchase from the co-operative.

Stock Check Confirms Grain Records Across Four Storage Sites

KESTREL BAY, Kestria, Oct. 22, 2026 /KestriaWire/ -- Prairie Gold Grain Co-operative has completed its autumn stock check at Amberford, Ostara, Kestrel Bay and Val-Brume. Measured stocks at the close of 21 October totalled 121,460 tonnes of wheat and 34,280 tonnes of oats. The figures include grain already allocated to customers but awaiting collection.

Staff compared bin measurements with receiving tickets, dispatch weights and recorded cleaning losses. The combined difference between measured grain and stock records was 0.08 per cent, within the co-operative's internal tolerance of 0.20 per cent. All four sites completed checks, and no unexplained difference required a customer allocation to be changed.

Routine temperature readings also found no storage parcel above the co-operative's action threshold of 20 degrees. Store teams continue to check grain condition and record aeration work. Customers requesting available volumes should contact the sales desk, as total physical stock includes committed grain and parcels held for further preparation.
